manualNotes.note: TWILIO CONTEXT: Budget is tight. Twilio costs $20 to start + ~$3/month for SMS volume. Owner needs to decide if this is worth it now vs later.
END GOAL: Best lead generation machine in the garage door market. Then copy-paste to Tampa, Orlando, Miami, and expand to HVAC, plumbing, locksmith verticals.
ADHD ACCOUNTABILITY: Tal has ADHD. All recommendations must be specific, focused, one thing at a time. Weekly north star metric. No overwhelm. Momentum is critical — small wins compound.

BUSINESS MODEL EVOLUTION: Phase 1 = personal lead gen. Phase 2 = sell leads to other techs. Phase 3 = license the full platform as vertical SaaS to other cities and services. The system must be built for leads from day one.

TIMELINE: 3-6 months to build a fully automated lead machine. Month 1-2: close first jobs, refine system. Month 3-4: start selling leads to other techs. Month 5-6: vertical SaaS, license to other garage door companies.
BUDGET: ~$200/month total operating budget. Every dollar must justify itself.
OWNER PROFILE: Tal is a garage door technician working as sub-contractor. Currently doing jobs himself while building the system.

CORE STRATEGY — THE SLICE PHILOSOPHY: We do NOT compete with Precision Garage Door, OGD, or Overhead Door. We do not need to beat them. We do not want their whole market. We want ONE profitable slice of Jacksonville — 1-2% of the market is enough to build a real business. Big players are slow, expensive, and arrogant. We are fast, lean, and local. Our edge is speed of response, personal attention, and smart targeting (premium zips, property managers, HOAs, emergency jobs). Once we own one slice in Jacksonville, we copy the exact same playbook to Tampa, then Orlando, then Miami. We are building a replication machine — not a war against giants. The CFO must always evaluate decisions through this lens: does this help us own our slice faster, or does it try to beat everyone at once? Focused beats scattered every time.

CORE VALUES: (1) Speed — respond faster than every competitor. (2) Focus — one city, one slice, prove it, then replicate. (3) Honesty — we are a dispatch platform, we never overstate what we are. (4) Simplicity — if the owner can't explain it in one sentence, it's too complicated. (5) Momentum — small consistent wins beat big swings. A closed job today is worth more than a perfect strategy tomorrow.
